solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: I have to enter fight or surrender

indicators.note: to enter something is to go inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: a war is a fight on a grand scale
I've is the contraction of 'I have'

explanation.surface: Someone facing a stark choice: join the battle or give up.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe of I've is dropped, as usual in crosswords. 'Or' merely joins the wordplay to the definition, though it reads as a choice.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the voluntary giving up of a legal right or claim, a formal kind of relinquishment.

clue.text: Result of engagement in battle?

blocks.note: surface reading: the outcome of a clash between armies
setter's reading: an engagement to marry, made during wartime, whose result is a woman wed to a serviceman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Engagement' in a military context means a fight, but here it is a betrothal; the question mark flags the wordplay on that double sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who marries a serving soldier met during a conflict is the product of a wartime betrothal.

clue.text: Olympian‘s unscrupulous boxing tactic for opening

indicators.note: an opening is the very start, so only the initial letter of the word is wanted
to box something is to enclose it, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: without scruples, lacking moral principles
the first letter of 'tactic'

explanation.surface: An athlete at the Games is accused of dirty boxing tactics in the opening round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests an athlete, but it means one of the gods of Mount Olympus. 'Boxing' looks like the sport but is the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olympians were the Greek gods dwelling on Mount Olympus, deathless beings who never die.

clue.text: Retreat from former geek’s passion?

blocks.note: ex- means former, as in ex-wife
information technology, the stereotypical obsession of a computer geek

explanation.surface: A former nerd withdraws from what once consumed them.
explanation.walkthrough: IT stands for information technology; the question mark admits that a geek's passion is a jokey stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: To retreat is to withdraw or depart, and a departure or way out is the noun or verb meaning leave.

clue.text: In Paris, the writer and journalist will welcome spring to get stoned

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the outer letters receive a piece inside

blocks.note: the writer refers to the setter as 'I', which is je in French
a spring is a natural source of water, a well
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor, the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: A Parisian writer and a reporter plan to welcome the spring by getting high.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris' signals French, and the writer is the setter's 'I'. 'Stoned' suggests drugs, but here it means set with precious stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Something jewelled is decorated with gems, and 'stoned' can describe an object studded with precious stones.

clue.text: All you need to know is in this new play, I concede

definitions.text: All you need to know is in this

indicators.note: something new is a fresh arrangement, so these letters are made over in another order

blocks.note: the twelve letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A playwright admits the new drama covers everything worth knowing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'this', and the comma before 'I concede' is surface punctuation only.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference work covering every subject aims to contain the sum of human knowledge in one set of volumes.

clue.text: Birds flying from either end of museums

indicators.note: only one end portion is wanted, and the rest of the word is dropped
things flying are scattered about, so these letters land in a fresh order

blocks.note: the first four letters; the last four, EUMS, would work equally well

explanation.surface: Birds escaping out of either end of a museum building.
explanation.walkthrough: Either four-letter end of the word, front or back, holds the same letters, which is why the setter can say 'either end'. Ironically these birds cannot fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Emus are large flightless Australian ratites, close relatives of the ostrich.

clue.text: Fat jerk discovered where food is kept

indicators.note: uncovered, with its covering stripped off, so the outside letters go and the inside stays

blocks.note: lard is pig fat used in cooking
the inner letters once the outer two are removed

explanation.surface: An overweight lout is found raiding the pantry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discovered' reads as 'found out', but means its cover is taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A larder is a cool pantry or storeroom in a house for keeping provisions.

clue.text: Cowboy town foreshadows the end of rustler and trickster

indicators.note: an end is a final point, so just the closing letter is kept
to foreshadow is to come before, so one piece precedes the next

blocks.note: Dodge City, Kansas, the famous Wild West cattle town
the final letter of 'rustler'

explanation.surface: A Wild West town sees early signs of a cattle thief's and conman's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: Dodge City is the frontier town of Western legend; the clue asks for its first word only.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodger is a shifty, evasive person who lives by tricks, like the Artful Dodger in Oliver Twist.

clue.text: Continue to avoid eastern part of Red Sea

indicators.note: on a map east is the right side, so the right-hand end of the word is shunned and dropped

blocks.note: the word without its final, rightmost letter
the main is an old poetic word for the open sea

explanation.surface: Navigational advice to keep away from the eastern stretch of the Red Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red Sea' looks like one place name, but the two words are clued separately; in an across clue, east is the end of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To remain is to stay on or carry on, so it is a synonym of persist or keep going.

clue.text: Got paper after a hundred died

indicators.note: coming after means following, so one piece is placed behind those before it

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a quire is a measure of paper, 24 or 25 sheets
d. is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: Someone bought a newspaper after a hundred people had died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' tempts as a newspaper, but it is the paper-trade measure QUIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquire is to obtain or come to possess something, the past tense matching the clue's verb.

clue.text: Host put illicit rum with my round

indicators.note: rum means odd or peculiar, so the letters end up in a strange order
going round something means encircling it, so these letters wrap the rest

blocks.note: taken as written, split to sit at each end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub landlord slips bootleg rum into a round of drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Host' looks like a landlord and 'rum' a drink, but the first is the definition and the second the anagram signal; 'round' puts MY around the result.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, a multitude, and multiplicity likewise means a large variety or number.

clue.text: Run time backwards — that’s unusual

indicators.note: going backwards means facing the other way, so these letters are written in the opposite direction

blocks.note: R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Running the clock backwards would be a remarkable event.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'time' is turned around; R stays at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare means seldom found or occurring, so it is a direct synonym of uncommon.

clue.text: Hasty Queen beheaded devil

indicators.note: losing the head means losing the top, so the first letter is cut off

blocks.note: Qu. is a standard abbreviation for queen
Old Nick is the devil; drop the first letter

explanation.surface: An impetuous queen has a demon executed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beheaded' seems to describe the queen, as with Anne Boleyn, but it applies to the devil that follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasty means done with speed or in a hurry, so fast or speedy fits it exactly.

clue.text: Surrender offspring in hearing

indicators.note: what is in hearing is listened to, so the word is judged by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: seed means offspring or descendants, as in biblical usage

explanation.surface: A parent gives up their child at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seed' for descendants is old-fashioned, as in 'Abraham and his seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up territory or rights formally, yielding them to another party.

clue.text: Losing head, grieve for heron

indicators.note: the head is the top or start, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: to regret is to grieve over something; drop the first letter

explanation.surface: Someone distraught mourns a heron.
explanation.walkthrough: The deletion applies to the synonym REGRET, not to 'grieve' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a white wading bird belonging to the heron family.

clue.text: Restrain degenerate coming after bishop

indicators.note: coming after means following behind, so that piece goes second

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for bishop
a rake is a dissolute, immoral man

explanation.surface: A bishop is urged to rein in the debauched man who follows him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' reads as a verb or adjective but is the noun for a dissolute person.
explanation.definitionFit: To brake is to slow or check movement, so it means hold back or curb.

clue.text: Endlessly windy poet’s taking over competition site

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter is cut away
to take something in is to hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: draughty means windy; drop its final letter
a bard is a poet
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A long-winded poet commandeers the venue of a contest.
explanation.walkthrough: Draughts is the British name for checkers, so the board is where a game of it is contested.
explanation.definitionFit: A draughtboard is the chequered playing surface on which two players compete at draughts (checkers).

clue.text: Run away, holding eleven billion litres in plastic

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it within, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to flee is to run away
XI is eleven in Roman numerals
b is the abbreviation for billion
l is the abbreviation for litres

explanation.surface: An escape from a sea of plastic carrying vast quantities of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plastic' looks like the material, but here it is the adjective meaning easily shaped.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic in its older sense means pliable and easily moulded, so bendy or supple matches it.

clue.text: Doris ate cooked starfish

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Doris dined on a cooked starfish.
explanation.walkthrough: The expected sense is a space rock; the zoological term is less familiar.
explanation.definitionFit: Asteroidea is the class of starfish, so in zoology an asteroid is a sea star.

clue.text: Occupies and destroys ability to influence others

blocks.note: to people a place is to inhabit or fill it
to kill is to destroy

explanation.surface: An invader that occupies and wrecks a country holds sway over others.
explanation.walkthrough: The word break in the answer falls one letter earlier than the join between the two verbs, so the enumeration hides the seam.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpersonal talents such as persuasion and tact are what let someone get on with and sway colleagues.

clue.text: Strike over hand getting fruit

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means placed above, so that piece comes first

blocks.note: to paw is to strike or scrape with a paw
paw is informal for a human hand

explanation.surface: Someone swats a hand away and grabs some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are the same word in two senses, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawpaw is another name for papaya, a tropical fruit, and also for a North American tree fruit.

clue.text: In light rain, doctor is fine to go out

indicators.note: saying one thing is another means it becomes that, so one piece swaps in for the other

blocks.note: drizzle is fine light rain
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A doctor declares it fine to go outside in a drizzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine' seems to mean 'all right', but supplies F, which takes the place of DR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that fizzles peters out or dies away, like a damp firework that fails to keep burning.

clue.text: Around six, Bill is hungry

indicators.note: to go around something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: an ad is an advertisement, also called a bill or poster
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Bill gets peckish at about six o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it is a poster or advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hungry can mean eager or keen for something, and avid shares that sense of strong desire.

clue.text: Poet removing king’s watch

indicators.note: removing means taking away, so a letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: Virgil, the Roman poet who wrote the Aeneid
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A poet takes the king's timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining wordplay to definition; 'watch' is not a timepiece but a period of keeping guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigil is a period of staying awake to keep guard or pray, a night watch.

clue.text: Pivot left in chopper

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an axe is a chopping tool
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A helicopter's pivot was left inside it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chopper' suggests a helicopter, but it is a cutting tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod on which a wheel turns, the central shaft it rotates around.

clue.text: In abandoned rehearsal sent back crowd

indicators.note: what is in something lies within it, so the letters are found inside the words
something sent back returns the way it came, so it reads in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letters across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A crowd sent home from a cancelled rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second, and must then be read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: A herd is a large group of animals, and by extension a mass of people or a throng.

clue.text: Trick Jack with copy

blocks.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
to ape is to imitate

explanation.surface: Fool Jack with an imitation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a person's name but is the playing card abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A jape is a practical joke or prank, a playful piece of mischief.

clue.text: Restaurant‘s pie containing two mystery ingredients, right one appetising at first

indicators.note: something containing another holds it within, so one piece wraps around
at first points to the start, so only the initial letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
unknowns in algebra are X, Y and Z, so two of them give Z twice
R is the abbreviation for right
I is one in Roman numerals
the first letter of 'appetising'

explanation.surface: A restaurant pie has two secret ingredients, one of them tempting enough at first taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mystery ingredients' are mathematical unknowns, conventionally X, Y or Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A pizzeria is an eatery specialising in pizza, which is a kind of open pie.

clue.text: Yogi’s follower pushing out two ducks to get in the morning grass

indicators.note: pushing something out forces it from its place so another can take it

blocks.note: Boo-Boo is the small bear who follows Yogi Bear in the cartoons
a duck is a zero score in cricket, shaped like O
a.m. denotes the morning

explanation.surface: A yoga master's disciple drives two ducks away to eat grass at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yogi' suggests a meditating guru, but it is the cartoon Yogi Bear, whose sidekick is Boo-Boo; AM takes the place of the first pair of Os.
explanation.definitionFit: Bamboo is botanically a giant woody member of the grass family Poaceae.

clue.text: When Toughies come out, needing 25% extra time, feeble bewilderment may be heard

definitions.text: When Toughies come out, needing 25% extra time

indicators.note: what is heard is listened to, so the words are taken by their sound alone

blocks.note: feeble means weak
a daze is a state of bewilderment

explanation.surface: A Toughie solver, needing a quarter more time, mutters in confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Telegraph Toughie ran Tuesday to Friday, four days; adding 25% gives the five days Monday to Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: The working days of the week are five, a quarter more than the four days the Toughie appears.

clue.text: Count departs terminus

blocks.note: the first three letters, as used for departures on a railway timetable
a terminus is an end point

explanation.surface: A railway timetable entry: the count is leaving from the terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman or a tally, but it is the verb as in 'count on'.
explanation.definitionFit: To count on someone is to rely on them, so the verb carries the sense of rely, as in 'count on me'.
